text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is determined by the formula: Blood Pressure = Cardiac Output x Total Peripheral Resistance. Cardiac output refers to the amount of blood the heart pumps per minute, while total peripheral resistance is the resistance to blood flow offered by the blood vessels.
snippet_highlighted_words: Blood Pressure = Cardiac Output x Total Peripheral Resistance

list.title: Cardiac Output (CO):
list.snippet: This is the volume of blood pumped by the heart per minute. It's calculated by multiplying the heart rate (HR) by the stroke volume (SV), which is the amount of blood ejected with each heartbeat: CO = HR x SV.

list.title: Total Peripheral Resistance (TPR):
list.snippet: This is the resistance that blood vessels offer to the flow of blood. It's influenced by the diameter of the blood vessels and the viscosity of the blood.

list.title: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP):
list.snippet: While not directly part of the main formula, MAP is a clinically relevant value derived from systolic and diastolic blood pressure. It represents the average arterial pressure during a single cardiac cycle. A common formula to estimate MAP is: MAP = (2 * Diastolic Pressure + Systolic Pressure) / 3 or MAP = Diastolic Pressure + 1/3 (Systolic Pressure - Diastolic Pressure).
